glb_reimport.method: Fresh Blender process with --factory-startup imported the final GLB via bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf; assertions checked hierarchy and decoded all six embedded images. No .blend was saved.
glb_reimport.test_setup_note: The first temporary helper run retained factory startup content and failed its all-images-packed assertion. The helper was corrected to explicitly clear the factory scene with read_factory_settings(use_empty=True), then the same unchanged final artifact imported successfully; this was a test setup correction.

limitations: This Blockout prepares later web interaction; it does not implement browser camera dragging, video direction switching, brightness/audio crossfades, or DOM explanations.

The main .blend uses the native source lion: 23 unique mesh objects and all 18 native hair-curve objects. Fifteen independently documented coincident mesh copies and three source lights are omitted; the user's original source is unchanged.
Render composition, model visibility, dark-room balance and reference fidelity require the separate visual review of the actual five preview images.

visual_review.method: Viewed all five final PNG files returned by the local image viewer after numerical verification. This manual review is separate from automated Blender API checks.
observations: Front: full lion including paws is visible; central stage, large primary screen, dim side screens, dark red pillars and one drum establish the intended hierarchy.
Left and Right: full profile, body, legs and native tail hair remain visible; four original source paw heights are preserved without deforming the model.
Back: rear view and full native tail are readable without clipping.

Overview: the 360-degree equirectangular diagnostic view shows four physical screen walls surrounding one stage; the Tuqiu rear screen is split across the left/right panorama seam, not duplicated as a fifth screen.

The room remains dark; brown-black stone has restrained soft highlights rather than water-like mirror reflections; no extra screens, lantern clusters, luminous floor patterns or visible debug geometry appear.
All four screens are explicitly labeled Blockout placeholders; these renders do not demonstrate real video playback or automatic view-direction switching.
